best_architecture: Recommended pattern for Local-Claw: an event-stream-driven ReAct loop with an optional upfront planning pass (ReAct+Plan hybrid) and Reflexion-style self-correction on failure, all running on an explicit state graph with durable checkpointing. Concretely, adopt the OpenHands/CodeAct design as the backbone: the agent is a `step(state) -> action` function over a chronological event stream of (action, observation) pairs, where actions are executable code/tool calls (bash, python via IPython, file edits) rather than ad-hoc JSON tool schemas. CodeAct (executable-code actions) outperforms text/JSON action formats because the LLM emits code it was heavily pretrained on and a single action can compose control flow, which matters for a smaller local brain like Gemma 4 / Qwen2.5-Coder-32B. Layer three loop refinements on top: (1) ReAct (Thought->Action->Observation interleaving) as the per-step inner loop for grounded, low-cost tool use; (2) a lightweight upfront Plan-Execute-Monitor wrapper that decomposes the task into subtasks before execution — empirically a ReAct+Plan hybrid beats both vanilla ReAct (83% -> 95% on a CTF coding study) and pure Tree-of-Thoughts, which is ~100x more compute and did NOT surpass ReAct+Plan, so AVOID full ToT search as the default for a local/compute-constrained agent and reserve branching search only for hard isolated subproblems; (3) Reflexion as the error-recovery layer — on test/build failure, an evaluator scores the result and a self-reflection module writes a natural-language diagnosis into an episodic memory buffer that is fed back into the next attempt, with a max-iterations cap. Key design decisions that matter most, in priority order: (a) Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) quality — SWE-Agent's central finding is that purpose-built, concise tools (scoped file viewer with line numbers, syntax-checking edit command, search_file/search_dir) dominate raw shell access; invest here before tuning prompts. (b) Sandboxed execution — run all actions in a Docker/container runtime with a persistent bash + python (IPython) kernel so state carries across steps. (c) State as the core abstraction — model the loop as an explicit graph (nodes = agent/tool/checkpoint, edges = transitions) with per-thread checkpointing so a multi-step coding task can pause for human approval, survive crashes/timeouts, and resume or time-travel/replay; this is exactly what LangGraph provides and what AutoGen lacks natively. (d) Context management via a repo map — use a Tree-sitter ranked-symbol graph (Aider's approach) so the agent requests only relevant files instead of stuffing the whole repo into a limited local context window. (e) Separation of reasoning and editing — Aider's architect/editor split (one model proposes, one converts to precise edit blocks) improves real-world refactor quality and lets Local-Claw use Gemma 4 as architect and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B as the editor (or vice versa). (f) Bounded loops with explicit termination — cap turns, detect unproductive loops (ReAct's known myopia/error-propagation failure mode), and always git-commit each successful edit so every step is a recoverable checkpoint. For Local-Claw specifically, map this onto your Python asyncio orchestrator: the ReAct/Plan-Execute-Monitor loop is the inner step function, MCP stdio tools are the action space (wrapped as a SWE-Agent-style ACI), MongoDB/Chroma/Redis back the Reflexion episodic memory + long-term memory, and a LangGraph-style checkpointer (or a custom asyncio checkpoint written to Mongo/Redis) provides resume/replay.
reference_papers: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al. 2023) - arxiv:2210.01702 - ICLR 2023; the canonical Thought-Action-Observation interleaved loop, foundational for SWE-Agent and most coding agents

Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning (Shinn et al. 2023) - arxiv:2303.11366 - NeurIPS 2023; actor/evaluator/self-reflection cycle with episodic memory for self-correcting code generation

Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models (Yao et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.10601 - NeurIPS 2023; thoughts as search-tree nodes with BFS/DFS; high compute, use selectively not as default coding loop

Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (Wang et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.04091 - ACL 2023; front-loaded plan-then-execute, basis for the Plan-Execute-Monitor decomposition

SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering (Yang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2405.15793 - NeurIPS 2024; ACI design (scoped editor/viewer/search tools) in a ReAct loop, SOTA on SWE-bench

OpenHands (OpenDevin): An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents (Wang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2407.16741 - ICLR 2025; event-stream agent abstraction, CodeActAgent, AgentDelegateAction multi-agent orchestration
Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents / CodeAct (Wang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2402.01030 - ICML 2024; argues executable code as the unified action space beats text/JSON actions

The OpenHands Software Agent SDK: A Composable and Extensible Foundation for Production Agents (2025) - arxiv:2511.03690 - V1 SDK; remote sandboxed execution, multi-LLM routing, action-level security, state synchronization

AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents (Liu et al. 2023) - arxiv:2308.03688 - ICLR 2024; 8-environment benchmark; identifies poor long-term reasoning/decision-making/instruction-following as main agent failure modes
reference_repos: All-Hands-AI/OpenHands - generalist software-developer agent platform (formerly OpenDevin); event-stream step() abstraction, CodeActAgent, Docker sandbox runtime, multi-agent delegation; MIT license, the most directly reusable architecture - https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands

SWE-agent/SWE-agent - Princeton agent with a purpose-built Agent-Computer Interface (scoped file editor/viewer/search) in a ReAct loop; reference for tool design over raw shell - https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent

Aider-AI/aider - terminal AI pair programmer; Tree-sitter repo map (ranked symbol graph), architect/editor two-model mode, git-native auto-commit per edit, model-agnostic; great for context management and edit-format strategy - https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider

langchain-ai/langgraph - graph-based agent runtime with native checkpointing, durable execution, thread-isolated state, human-in-the-loop, and time-travel/replay; v1.0 (late 2025); strongest fit for Plan-Execute-Monitor + resume - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph
noahshinn/reflexion - official Reflexion implementation; actor/evaluator/self-reflection loop with episodic memory for coding and reasoning tasks - https://github.com/noahshinn/reflexion
princeton-nlp/tree-of-thought-llm - official Tree of Thoughts (NeurIPS 2023) implementation with BFS/DFS search over thoughts - https://github.com/princeton-nlp/tree-of-thought-llm
THUDM/AgentBench - comprehensive LLM-as-agent benchmark across 8 interactive environments (ICLR 2024); useful for evaluating Local-Claw's loop - https://github.com/THUDM/AgentBench

microsoft/autogen - conversational multi-agent framework; strong for multi-agent debate/review but weak native state/checkpointing - reference for the multi-agent collaboration pattern only - https://github.com/microsoft/autogen
